full_judgment: 14. This article 3 is nothing but the reproduction of section 3 of the trade marks Invalidation and Summary Registration Act, 1950. The said section 3 was considered in the case reported in PLD 1962 Karachi 355. It was provided in that section that the trade marks registered in India shall be deemed not to have been registered in Pakistan unless they have been applied for and registered under that Act. In that case the trade mark "Nabisco" was not registered in Pakistan by any party. This trade mark was registered in India on behalf of the respondent. It was held that the registration of the trade mark in India had no legal value in Pakistan in view of provisions of section 3 of the trade marks Invalidation and Summary Registration Act, 1950. So is the case here. The trade mark "BALLY" of the appellant was registered in Pakistan. But after the emergence of Bangladesh the appellant had neither applied for nor got their trade mark summarily registered under Article 6 of President's Order 19 of 1973 and as such it must be deemed not to have been registered in Bangladesh at any point of time till to-day.
